syllabus_extract: Video demonstrating fluid flow characteristics. Video on theory of flight Lift (b) Drag (c) control.
specific_objectives: 6.1.1.1 Trainee will be able to explain the properties of atmosphere, flow over bodies, boundary layer.

training_aids.remarks: Refer to the master syllabus reference list
Objective: teach the syllabus extract for this lesson

practical: Review video segments; Instructor supervises note-taking on flow separation and boundary layer concepts.
intro_questions: What are the three primary forces acting on an aircraft in flight?
Define the boundary layer in the context of fluid flow over a body.
List two properties of the atmosphere relevant to aerodynamic performance.

development.content:
Properties of Atmosphere
Flow Over Bodies
Boundary Layer Formation
Flow Separation
Viscosity Effects

Lift Generation Principles
Drag Components Analysis
Control Surface Mechanics
Pressure Distribution
Angle of Attack Effects

Interrelation of Forces
Stability Characteristics
Performance Implications
Flow Visualization
Real-world Applications

summary_questions: Explain how the boundary layer affects drag on an aircraft body.
Describe the relationship between angle of attack and lift coefficient.
Identify the primary control surfaces used for pitch, roll, and yaw.
home_assignment_question: Prepare a brief note on how the concepts of lift and drag discussed in this lesson will be expanded upon in LP 11 regarding factors affecting the coefficient of lift.

pft_rows.syllabus: Factors affecting CL, Theories of Lift production, force and pitching moment, coefficient of lift, variation of co-efficient of lift with aspect ratio and sweep back and CL.
